Keynote

Concept 6 · Direction: Apple-inspired: product storytelling

Borrows the structure of an Apple product page and applies it to the whole shop: a three-line statement (trolleys, fitted clubs, free fitting) over a spot-lit M5 GPS DHC, then a row of large highlight cards that explain the range in four facts drawn from the catalogue (GPS, downhill control, remote, 18 or 36 holes). Three huge numbers carry the proof: £0 fitting, the 1pm next-day cut-off and the £60.90 membership saving. A four-column compare row (SE, M1, M5 GPS DHC, M7 GPS Remote) is the ‘which one?’ moment. The page then turns light for fitting, the one human section, before going dark again for clubs and membership.

Structural changes from the brief’s section order

The hero carries all three specialisms in its headline. Pillars are replaced by highlight cards; the trolley carousel becomes a four-model compare; the trust row becomes ‘in numbers’. Fitting is the single light section, so it stands out. Reviews, guides and secondary categories are condensed into a three-column tail.

Imagery and photography

Spot-lit product shots on black: the trolley as the star, with a soft radial light behind it. Highlight cards use the Motocaddy gallery images that already show the GPS screen, DHC dial and remote. One documentary photo for fitting.

Headline copy

H1: “Motocaddy trolleys. Fitted clubs. Free fitting.”

Sections: “Get to know the range.” · “Which Motocaddy is right for you?” · “Fitting, explained.” · “Pays for itself.”

Motion

The most motion of any concept: the trolley fades up out of black on load, highlight cards slide horizontally, numbers count up once. All of it switched off under ‘reduce motion’.

Trade-offs

Does wellThe most dramatic and memorable; the compare row is the clearest ‘which trolley?’ tool for a first-time buyer; highlight cards teach the range without a wall of specs.
Weaker onDark pages can feel cold and are harder for older eyes; long scroll on mobile; only four trolleys compared on the homepage; the cinematic feel needs better trolley renders than the current gallery shots.
Build effortMedium: scroll-linked animation and a compare component; every third-party widget needs dark styling.
Photography neededMedium: proper studio renders of the trolleys on black would make it; one fitting photo.
Suits bestTrolley buyers deciding between models; visitors who arrive curious and have time to scroll.

EG monogram: No monogram in the nav; the wordmark ‘Evolution Golf’ in Inter Semibold, silver on black (suggestion only; the mark itself isn’t being redesigned here).
